skill.name: circleci-automation
skill.description: Automate CircleCI tasks through Rube MCP, including pipeline triggers, workflow monitoring, job inspection, artifacts, and test metadata.
skill.summary: Use Rube MCP to trigger CircleCI pipelines, monitor workflows, inspect jobs, and review build outputs.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All static external command findings are false positives caused by markdown inline code or fenced examples that name Rube and CircleCI tools. The only URL is the disclosed Rube MCP endpoint, and the reconnaissance alerts refer to CircleCI workflow operations rather than host discovery. No prompt injection attempt or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Side-effecting CircleCI actions are described without an explicit confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to confirm project slug, branch or tag, parameters, and expected impact before calling CIRCLECI_TRIGGER_PIPELINE.

remediation.issue: The third-party MCP trust boundary is only briefly described.
remediation.suggestion: State that users should authorize Rube MCP only for intended CircleCI scopes and review artifact data before sharing it.

static_findings.snippet: - Active CircleCI connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `circleci`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
1. `CIRCLECI_TRIGGER_PIPELINE` - Trigger a new pipeline on a project [Required]
- `branch`: Git branch to run the pipeline on
- `tag`: Git tag to run the pipeline on (mutually exclusive with branch)
- `branch` and `tag` are mutually exclusive; providing both causes an error
- Pipeline parameters must match those defined in `.circleci/config.yml`
1. `CIRCLECI_LIST_PIPELINES_FOR_PROJECT` - List recent pipelines for a project [Required]
- `page_token`: Pagination cursor for next page of results
- `page_token` is returned in responses for pagination; continue until absent
2. `CIRCLECI_GET_JOB_ARTIFACTS` - List all artifacts from the job [Required]
- Each artifact has a `path` and `url` for download
- Failed tests include failure messages in the `message` field
- Pass token as `page_token` in next request
- Continue until `next_page_token` is absent or null
- Must include VCS prefix: `gh/` for GitHub, `bb/` for Bitbucket
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- Avoid rapid polling; use reasonable intervals (5-10 seconds)

content.user_title: Automate CircleCI Pipelines and Job Checks
content.value_statement: Teams lose time switching between CI dashboards and assistants. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through CircleCI actions using Rube MCP.
actual_capabilities: Connects to CircleCI through Rube MCP and checks current tool schemas.
Triggers CircleCI pipelines with project slugs, branches, tags, and parameters.
Lists pipelines and workflows, including pagination and status handling.
Retrieves job details, artifacts, and test metadata for completed jobs.
Explains CircleCI ID formats, project slug formats, and common API pitfalls.
limitations: Requires an active Rube MCP connection and an authorized CircleCI account.
Does not manage CircleCI credentials or bypass access controls.
Depends on current CircleCI and Rube tool schemas at run time.
Artifact downloads may need authentication and may be subject to size limits.

use_cases.title: Run a release pipeline
use_cases.description: Trigger a CircleCI pipeline for a selected branch or tag, then monitor the resulting workflows.

use_cases.title: Debug a failed job
use_cases.description: Inspect job details, retrieve artifacts, and review test metadata for a failed build.

use_cases.title: Review CI health
use_cases.description: List recent pipelines and workflow states to understand current project build status.

prompt_templates.title: Check pipeline status
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner status check for one project branch.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to check recent CircleCI pipelines for gh/example/app on main. Search Rube tools first, then summarize pipeline and workflow states.

prompt_templates.title: Trigger a pipeline
prompt_templates.scenario: Run a normal CI build after confirming target details.
prompt_templates.prompt: Trigger a CircleCI pipeline for gh/example/app on branch main with no parameters. Confirm the project slug and branch before starting it.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose test failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate failing jobs from a known pipeline.
prompt_templates.prompt: For pipeline ID 5034460f-c7c4-4c43-9457-de07e2029e7b, list workflows, find failed jobs, retrieve test metadata, and summarize the failures.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a release run
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced release check across trigger, monitoring, and artifacts.
prompt_templates.prompt: For gh/example/api, start a staging release pipeline with approved parameters, monitor workflows with reasonable polling, list artifacts, and flag any blocker.

output_examples.input: Check the latest CircleCI pipeline for gh/acme/api on main.
output_examples.output: Latest pipeline is running. Two workflows are active: build is running, and integration tests are pending. Check again after 10 seconds.
Job 123 completed with failures. Test metadata shows three failed tests in the payment suite, with assertion messages available.
The job produced coverage, test report, and build bundle artifacts. Download links may require CircleCI authentication.

best_practices: Confirm the project slug and target branch before triggering a pipeline.
Call RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS before using CircleCI tools because schemas can change.
Use reasonable polling intervals and stop when workflows reach terminal states.
anti_patterns: Do not trigger production pipelines without explicit user confirmation.
Do not assume job numbers and pipeline IDs use the same format.
Do not expose artifact URLs or failure messages outside the authorized workspace.

faq.question: What connection does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires Rube MCP and an active CircleCI connection authorized by the user.

faq.question: Can it trigger new CircleCI runs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide the assistant to trigger pipelines for a project, branch, tag, and supported parameters.

faq.question: Can it inspect failed jobs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can retrieve job details, artifacts, and uploaded test metadata when CircleCI provides them.

faq.question: Does it store CircleCI credentials?
faq.answer: No. The skill only documents tool usage. Authentication is handled through Rube MCP and CircleCI authorization.

faq.question: Which project slug format should I use?
faq.answer: Use the CircleCI format with a VCS prefix, such as gh/org/repo for GitHub or bb/org/repo for Bitbucket.

faq.question: Can it download artifacts directly?
faq.answer: It can list artifact URLs. Direct downloads may require authentication and must respect project access rules.
